newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian unions challenge EU governments on jobs.
newsitem.headline: Belgian unions challenge EU governments on jobs.

text.p: Belgian trades union leaders told a mass rally of workers from all over Europe on Sunday they would no longer accept hollow promises from European Union governments on fighting mounting job losses.

"Today's demonstration is not the end. It is not the final act. Together united we will continue our struggle for a social Europe. For a Europe of solidarity," Michel Nollet, head of the Communist FGTB union, told the crowd of several thousand people.

Unions said 60,000 people were converging on Brussels from all over Europe for the March for Jobs sparked off by the shock announcement two weeks ago that French carmaker Renault was closing its Belgian plant with the loss of 3,100 jobs.

"The brutal and uncontrolled closure of Renault and of all the other companies forces us to demand the respect and also the stregnthening of the rules on closures and collective dismissals," Nollet told the crowd.
The unemployment rate in Europe is 10.8 percent.
Willy Peirens, head of the Christian Democrat CSC union, said workers had had enough.

"This is a signal af anger and indignation. A signal of solidarity against brutality. Why does our message always fall on deaf ears until we are overtaken by a social disaster. Until the bomb bursts," he said.
"Why are all the promises of today quietly forgotten tomorrow? We don't want to be lied to again. We won't be cheated again," he roared.
The crowd was awash with colour and noise, red and green union banners and balloons, ear-shattering whistles and firecrackers, chanting, sirens and megaphones.
A hanging effigy of Renault Chairman Louis Schweitzer was prominant among the banners.

"All together for a Social Europe of full employment," read one banner. "No to a Europe of money. For work and Social Europe" read another. "Bosses have the right to live well, workers can die" read yet another.
Unions said there were thousands of workers from France, and delegations from Spain, Portugal, Germany, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Italy, Greece, Austria, Hungary, Slovenia and the Czech Republic.
